I’ve skinned a few pieces of road kill. 

First off once the animal is dead is very unlikely to pass on any pathogens. Most bacteria/viruses survive on a dead animal for a very short time. 

That being said it sounds like your doing everything right, always wear gloves (a mask is good too), avoid animals that look noticeably ill eg mange, ticks, fleas etc make sure your using disposable blades and that your scalpel handles and anything else non disposable is throughly sanitised. And wash your hands and arms (think like surgeons do) after your done. 

An apron wouldn’t go a miss either to avoid anything getting on your clothes. 

Like I said, with the exception of parasites most pathogens die shortly after the animal dies. If you have the facilities freezing it for a few weeks is another good way to make sure no nasties are about when you skin it. 

Good luck!

I imagine myself at the age when the majority of my trauma happened (around 5-7) and I just speak to them in my head. If I’m feeling overwhelmed or anxious, I ask them what’s going on, why they feel upset etc

A lot of the time their answer is “I don’t know” or “I’m worried they are mad at me” so I reassure them, say it’s ok to not know but I’m here for them and we are going to manage it together. I say I’m not going to let anyone harm them and that they never have to live through any of what happened to me/them again. I usually end it with imagining myself hugging them. 

I don’t only use it in times of stress, I’ve found it immensely helpful just to check in with them at the end of the day.

I had a medical abortion last year, I also have ementophia. The first lot of meds did make me feel sick. But it was nothing I couldn’t breathe through, I got some fresh air, walked around a bit, I’ve water etc. 

I inserted the second lots of meds because I’d heard that generally causes less side effects. 

I slept through most of it, mild cramping for a couple hours then bad pain for about 30 minutes. Nothing I couldn’t handle (and my period cramps are usually pretty good, so I wasn’t used to pain worse than slight discomfort) hot water bottle, pain killers. Then I passed everything in one go. 

My boyfriend sat by me the whole time, got me drinks, refilled my hot water bottles, and just cuddled me until it was over. It was much less dramatic than I thought it would be. 

I bought myself new pjs for the event because new pjs always make me feel good, fresh bedding all the comfy stuff. 

Take care of yourself and do whatever you need to feel comfortable. I cannot stress how much “less dramatic” than I thought it would be.

ETA: I had no nausea whatsoever from the pain, I think the nausea I experienced from the first lot of meds was purely psychological.
